title: Choosing shoes to reduce foot pain
publisher: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust
claims: About 1 cm space between the end of the longest toe and the end of the shoe is ideal.
The front of the shoe needs to be deep enough not to press on the tops of the toes.
Narrow or pointed shoes can squash the feet and over time cause nail problems, corns or nerve damage.
Laces or Velcro allow the shoe to be fastened on the arch of the foot, which allows enough space for the toes to function properly.
Slip-on shoes hold on by fitting tightly round the toes, which can cause pain and pressure at the forefoot.
Shop at the end of the day so the feet are at their largest if they tend to swell.
